<!-- plain-summary -->
The TiKV backend has ready-made docker deployment recipes: a tiny single-node testbed, a multi-replica cluster that can have faults injected into it, and the canonical "small multi-node" single-zone stack (PR #457) that runs every Wyrd role against real backends — wired to TiKV. FoundationDB needs its own recipes at each of those three tiers, and the canonical stack in particular becomes **two peer setups**: one with TiKV, one with FoundationDB. Both stay runnable — TiKV is the retained fallback, FoundationDB the production track.

## What

FDB counterparts to the three TiKV deploy profiles under `deploy/` (ADR-0043 testing-fixture profiles; `deploy/` stays outside the Cargo workspace per ADR-0010, guarded by `xtask/tests/deploy_no_orchestrator_coupling.rs`):

1. **`deploy/fdb-single-node/`** — one `foundationdb` container (official image, current 7.3/7.4 stable line), first-boot init via `fdbcli --exec "configure new single memory"` (or ssd), the generated `fdb.cluster` file exposed to the host. This is the compose service #439 item 1 describes; it lives here so the deploy profiles are one directory, and #439's CI workflow + doctor rows consume it. Peer of `deploy/tikv-single-node/`.
2. **`deploy/fdb-multi-replica/`** — a 3-process FDB cluster (double/triple redundancy mode) plus the **fault-injection sidecar**, reusing the `iptables-agent` pattern from `deploy/tikv-multi-replica/` (it is a generic iptables sidecar, not TiKV-specific). This is the stack the #442 fault battery drives: kill `fdbserver` mid-commit, partition client↔cluster, induce 1021 `commit_unknown_result`. Peer of `deploy/tikv-multi-replica/`.
3. **The canonical single-zone stack becomes a TiKV/FDB pair.** `deploy/small-multi-node/` (PR #457; ADR-0043, M4.5 #256) is the ONE canonical minimum-viable single-zone topology — 3 etcd + 3 PD + 3 TiKV + 9 D servers + 3 custodians + 3 S3 gateways, image built `--features tikv,etcd`. It is TiKV-wired, and it **stays** (current default until #442 flips; retained-fallback posture per #443). Add the FDB peer as its own full setup:
   - **`deploy/small-multi-node-fdb/`** — identical role topology, with the PD+TiKV tier replaced by the FDB cluster (redundancy-mode replicated), wyrd services running `--metadata-backend fdb` (#440), image from #470 (the `wyrd:fdb` image, `--features fdb,etcd`).
   - **Naming**: once the FDB peer lands, rename the existing stack to **`deploy/small-multi-node-tikv/`** so the pair is explicit and neither reads as "the" stack by name; `deploy/README.md` states which one is canonical — TiKV until #442 records go, FDB after. (If the rename is deferred to avoid churning PR #457's landed paths, record that in the README instead; the requirement is two clearly-named peer setups.)
   - Two directories, not a compose override: the metadata tier swap is a whole service-set change, and the existing per-backend convention (`tikv-single-node/`, `tikv-multi-replica/`) already uses one directory per backend profile.

## Acceptance criteria

- `docker compose up` in each of the two new backend profiles (1, 2) yields a healthy cluster from a clean checkout (`fdbcli --exec "status minimal"` reports healthy).
- The fault sidecar in `fdb-multi-replica` can partition and heal named links on demand, same operator surface as the tikv profile.
- **Both** small-multi-node setups bring every role up: the TiKV one keeps its current behavior unchanged; the FDB one reaches the same smoke bar — an S3 gateway answers with `--metadata-backend fdb` end to end (the full closed write path remains #455's demonstration).
- `deploy/README.md` documents the full profile matrix (single-node, multi-replica, small-multi-node × TiKV/FDB), which profile each test suite (conformance, battery, first-deployment gate) targets, and which small-multi-node setup is currently canonical.
- The `deploy_no_orchestrator_coupling` guard still passes.

## Sequencing

Depends on #438 (driver) and #470 (the `wyrd:fdb` image); profile 1 can land alongside #439. Profile 2 blocks #442's fault battery; the small-multi-node-fdb setup blocks the post-go default flip and the #367 gate rerun (which, after go, runs against the FDB setup while the TiKV setup remains the fallback's runnable proof, #443/#471). Targets `main` after `feat/m4-production-metadata-backend` merges.

comments.body: Rescoped after review: `deploy/small-multi-node/` (PR #457) is TiKV-wired, and the requirement is **two peer setups** of the canonical single-zone stack — one with TiKV (stays; current default and the retained fallback per #443) and one with FoundationDB (`small-multi-node-fdb`, the production track) — not an FDB variant/override of a single stack. Body updated: two directories, explicit pair naming (`small-multi-node-tikv` / `small-multi-node-fdb`), README states which is canonical (TiKV until #442 records go, FDB after).

milestone.title: Metadata Store FoundationDB
milestone.description: Production distributed MetadataStore backend on FoundationDB — the chosen production backend per ADR-0042. metadata-fdb behind the fdb feature (implementation-first per ADR-0002; contract docs consolidated afterwards in #437), libfdb_c packaging + wyrd:fdb image, dev/CI harness, deploy profiles, go/no-go fault+contention battery, and the TiKV development stand-down once FDB is the default. (Renamed from metadata-client.)

title: Deploy: FDB profiles — fdb-single-node, fdb-multi-replica + fault agent, and the small-multi-node TiKV/FDB peer setups
